title: Boolean counter loop run to escape
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes and distinct states $a$ and $e$. Let $w$ be a Boolean word, and suppose the extra tape initially agrees with the word buffer at cells $cp+p$ for every integer $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$. Given an initial configuration $c$, a run-length function $\\tau$, and an index $r_0$ strictly below the binary value of $w$, suppose every round $r\\le r_0$ starts in state $a$, has positive length, and all positive-time intermediate states differ from both $a$ and $e$. Suppose the configuration after round $r_0$ has state $e$. If $T$ is the sum of the round lengths for $r\\le r_0$ plus $\\operatorname{overhead}(w,r_0+1)$, then the Boolean counter-loop machine reaches its escape configuration at time $T$, with the extra tape holding the counter word after $r_0+1$ decrements. Before $T$ its state is neither done nor escape; through $T$ its extra head lies in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and its first $k$ head positions match those of some run of $M$ from a round configuration, with either $r\\le r_0$ and $u\\le\\tau(c_r)$ or $r=r_0+1$ and $u=0$.
